page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 256 GB, aligning with the standard general-purpose distribution of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU.

A key architectural component of the instance is the provision of 3800 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. This integrated instance volume offers high-throughput, low-latency disk access for data-intensive operations directly on the physical host, removing dependence on network-attached block devices. In addition, the system delivers a 67 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, ensuring ample network headroom for high-volume inter-node communication, distributed clustering, and large-scale external data transfers.

The bundled NVMe capacity provides strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for input- and output-intensive operations by eliminating the overhead of external storage provisioning. Because instance store volumes are ephemeral, applications requiring persistence must account for software-level replication. Given its balance of dedicated compute, high memory, rapid local NVMe storage, and substantial network capacity, the m8idb.16xlarge is suited for operational databases, distributed caching layers, batch data processing pipelines, search indexing, and high-concurrency web application backends.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance configured on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs spanning 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The system includes 256 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include 3800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, eliminating off-instance storage latency for input- and output-heavy operations. Networking is backed by a 67 Gbps baseline bandwidth, supporting high-throughput cluster traffic and continuous data ingest. By coupling high-capacity local flash storage with dense compute and networking, the instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense enterprise environments. The m8idb.16xlarge fits relational databases, NoSQL datastores, distributed caching systems, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-traffic web applications.
